
## 🔍 Quick sanity check before correlation

Always inspect your data first:
```{r}
head(students)
str(students)
summary(students)
```
## And check missing values:

```{r}
sum(is.na(students$Avg_Daily_Usage_Hours))
sum(is.na(students$Mental_Health_Score))
```
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(students, aes(x = Avg_Daily_Usage_Hours, y = Mental_Health_Score)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "Social Media Usage vs Mental Health Score",
       x = "Avg Daily Usage (Hours)",
       y = "Mental Health Score (1–10)")
```



## Survey sanity check
```{r}
cor.test(students$Avg_Daily_Usage_Hours, students$Mental_Health_Score)
```
# Dreaddit stress model | Train 1 baseline classifier

## 1. Load Dreaddit (stress dataset)

File you said: Data/dreaddit-test.csv

```{r}
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)

dreaddit <- fread("Data/dreaddit-test.csv")

# Check data
dim(dreaddit)
str(dreaddit)
table(dreaddit$label)
```

## 🧹 2. Remove columns not usable directly in baseline

We avoid text at this step — use only engineered LIWC features.

```{r}
dreaddit_clean <- dreaddit %>%
  select(-text, -subreddit, -post_id, -sentence_range) %>% 
  mutate(label = factor(label))
```

## 🧪 3. Train/Test Split

```{r}
set.seed(123)

train_idx <- sample(1:nrow(dreaddit_clean), 0.8 * nrow(dreaddit_clean))
train <- dreaddit_clean[train_idx, ]
test  <- dreaddit_clean[-train_idx, ]
```

## 🤖 4. Train Logistic Regression (baseline model)

We train on all LIWC features automatically:

```{r}
library(caret)

model <- train(
  label ~ ., 
  data = train,
  method = "glm",
  family = "binomial"
)
```

## 📊 5. Evaluation
Predictions
```{r}
pred <- predict(model, newdata = test)
```

## Confusion Matrix

```{r}
confusionMatrix(pred, test$label)
```
## ROC-AUC

```{r}
library(pROC)

prob <- predict(model, newdata = test, type = "prob")[,2]
roc_curve <- roc(test$label, prob)
auc(roc_curve)
```
🧠 6. Feature Importance (psycholinguistic markers):

```{r}
importance <- varImp(model)
print(importance)
plot(importance, top = 20)
```

```{r}
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "data.table", "stringr", "textclean", "tm"))
```

✅ Step 2: Read a sample of tweets

(We will sample 10k to start — Mendeley has ~548k)

```{r}
library(readxl)

tweets <- read_excel("Data/Mendeley/Tweet_Contents.xlsx")  # modify path if needed
tweets <- as.data.table(tweets)
# Sample the data table using the correct sample size
tweets <- tweets[sample(.N, sample_size)]

# Check the dimensions of the new tweets object
dim(tweets)


tweets <- tweets[sample(.N, 10000)]  # Random 10k rows
colnames(tweets) <- c("tweet")   # rename if needed
head(tweets)
```

```{r}
library(textclean)
library(tm)
library(stringr)

clean_tweet <- function(text) {
  text %>%
    tolower() %>%                                         # lowercase
    replace_url() %>%                                     # remove URLs
    str_replace_all("@[A-Za-z0-9_]+", "") %>%             # remove mentions
    str_replace_all("#[A-Za-z0-9_]+", "") %>%             # remove hashtags
    replace_emoji("") %>%                                 # remove emojis
    replace_html() %>%                                    # remove HTML entities
    str_replace_all("[^a-zA-Z\\s]", " ") %>%              # remove non-text
    removeNumbers() %>%                                   # remove numbers
    removePunctuation() %>%                               # remove punctuation
    removeWords(stopwords("en")) %>%                      # remove stopwords
    stripWhitespace()                                     # trim spaces
}
```



```{r}
library(textclean)
library(tm)
library(stringr)

clean_tweet <- function(text) {
  text %>%
    tolower() %>%                                                   # lowercase
    replace_url() %>%                                               # remove URLs
    str_replace_all("@[A-Za-z0-9_]+", "") %>%                       # remove mentions
    str_replace_all("#[A-Za-z0-9_]+", "") %>%                       # remove hashtags
    
    # FIX: Use stringr::str_replace_all() to remove emojis 
    # This pattern targets most standard emoji blocks for removal
    # (The original textclean::replace_emoji() was the source of the error)
    str_replace_all(., "[^\\p{L}\\p{N}\\s\\p{P}]+", "") %>% 
    
    replace_html() %>%                                              # remove HTML entities
    str_replace_all("[^a-zA-Z\\s]", " ") %>%                        # remove non-text (already handled by the fix, but kept for redundancy)
    removeNumbers() %>%                                             # remove numbers
    removePunctuation() %>%                                         # remove punctuation
    removeWords(stopwords("en")) %>%                                # remove stopwords
    stripWhitespace()                                               # trim spaces
}

# Then run your cleaning step again
tweets$clean_text <- sapply(tweets$tweet, clean_tweet)
head(tweets$clean_text)
```
## Cleaned Tweets Data :
```{r}
library(dplyr)

sample_n(data.frame(raw = tweets$tweet, clean = tweets$clean_text), 10)
```
